svg.title: The hormone-therapy edge shrank as the study grew
svg.desc: Weight loss on GLP-1 drugs in midlife women with versus without menopausal hormone therapy, from Mayo Clinic records. Semaglutide at 12 months: 16% vs 12% in a 2024 study of 106 women; 11.0% vs 9.5% in a 2026 study of 2,379 women (11.9% vs 10.9% at last follow-up). Tirzepatide: 19.2% vs 14.0% at last follow-up in a 2026 study of 120 women; in a cohort of 1,476 women, 6.6% vs 5.9% at 3 months and no significant difference at any later time. Observational, not randomized.

svg.text: In the 1,476-woman tirzepatide cohort, no time point after 3 months showed a significant gap.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Small studies (16 and 40 women on hormones) found gaps of 4 to 5 points; bigger ones, under 2.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Medical-record studies, not randomized: women who get hormones may differ from those who don’t in ways

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: matching can’t fully remove. Both 2026 cohorts kept only women who stayed on the drug at least 12 months.
